arxiv-2008-09890.title: Supervision Levels Scale (SLS)
arxiv-2008-09890.creator: Dima Damen, Michael Wray
arxiv-2008-09890.description: Abstract We propose a three-dimensional discrete and incremental scale to encode a method’s level of supervision — i.e. the data and labels used when training a model to achieve a given performance. We capture three aspects of supervision, that are known to give methods an advantage while requiring additional costs: pre-training, training labels and training data.

arxiv-2105-14768.title: Securing IoT Devices by Exploiting Backscatter Propagation Signatures
arxiv-2105-14768.creator: Zhiqing Luo, Wei Wang, Qianyi Huang, Tao Jiang, Qian Zhang
arxiv-2105-14768.description: Abstract The low-power radio technologies open up many opportunities to facilitate Internet-of-Things (IoT) into our daily life, while their minimalist design also makes IoT devices vulnerable to many active attacks. Recent advances use an antenna array to extract fine-grained physical-layer signatures to identify the attackers, which adds burdens in terms of energy and hardware cost to IoT devices.

arxiv-2112-02046.title: Hydrodynamics and transport in the long-range-interacting φ 4 \varphi^{4} chain
arxiv-2112-02046.creator: Stefano Iubini, Stefano Lepri, Stefano Ruffo
arxiv-2112-02046.description: Abstract We present a simulation study of the one-dimensional φ 4 \varphi^{4} lattice theory with long-range interactions decaying as an inverse power r − ( 1 + σ ) r^{-(1+\sigma)} of the intersite distance r r , σ > 0 \sigma>0 . We consider the cases of single and double-well local potentials with both attractive and repulsive couplings.

arxiv-2301-09755.title: Modeling Preferences: A Bayesian Mixture of Finite Mixtures for Rankings and Ratings
arxiv-2301-09755.creator: Michael Pearce a {a}, Elena A. Erosheva a ​ b ​ c {abc}
arxiv-2301-09755.description: Abstract Rankings and ratings are commonly used to express preferences but provide distinct and complementary information. Rankings give ordinal and scale-free comparisons but lack granularity; ratings provide cardinal and granular assessments but may be highly subjective or inconsistent. Collecting and analyzing rankings and ratings jointly has not been performed until recently due to a lack of principled methods.

arxiv-2306-08786.title: Deterministic and Work-Efficient Parallel Batch-Dynamic Trees in Low Span
arxiv-2306-08786.creator: Daniel Anderson, Guy E. Blelloch
arxiv-2306-08786.description: Abstract Dynamic trees are a well-studied and fundamental building block of dynamic graph algorithms dating back to the seminal work of Sleator and Tarjan [ STOC’81 , (1981), pp. 114-122]. The problem is to maintain a tree subject to online edge insertions and deletions while answering queries about the tree, such as the heaviest weight on a path, etc.

arxiv-2310-14139.title: Are LSTMs Good Few-Shot Learners? Thanks: Accepted at Machine Learning Journal, Special Issue of the ECML PKDD 2023 Journal Track
arxiv-2310-14139.creator: Mike Huisman, Thomas M. Moerland, Aske Plaat, Jan N. van Rijn
arxiv-2310-14139.description: Abstract Deep learning requires large amounts of data to learn new tasks well, limiting its applicability to domains where such data is available. Meta-learning overcomes this limitation by learning how to learn. In 2001, Hochreiter et al. showed that an LSTM trained with backpropagation across different tasks is capable of meta-learning.

arxiv-2401-13690.title: A generic model of consciousness
arxiv-2401-13690.creator: Mark Hadley
arxiv-2401-13690.description: Abstract This is a model of consciousness. The hard problem of consciousness, what it feels like, is answered. The work builds on medical research analyzing the source and mechanisms associated with our feelings. It goes further by describing a generic model with wide applicability.

arxiv-2409-06696.title: Cooptimizing Safety and Performance with a Control-Constrained Formulation
arxiv-2409-06696.creator: Hao Wang, Adityaya Dhande, Somil Bansal
arxiv-2409-06696.description: Abstract Autonomous systems have witnessed a rapid increase in their capabilities, but it remains a challenge for them to perform tasks both effectively and safely. The fact that performance and safety can sometimes be competing objectives renders the cooptimization between them difficult.

arxiv-2409-10677.title: Mitigating Sex Bias in Audio Data-driven COPD and COVID-19 Breathing Pattern Detection Models
arxiv-2409-10677.creator: Rachel Pfeifer 1, Sudip Vhaduri 2, James Eric Dietz 2
arxiv-2409-10677.description: Abstract In the healthcare industry, researchers have been developing machine learning models to automate diagnosing patients with respiratory illnesses based on their breathing patterns. However, these models do not consider the demographic biases, particularly sex bias, that often occur when models are trained with a skewed patient dataset.

arxiv-2411-15307.title: A p < 0.0001 p<0.0001 detection of CMB cooling in galactic halos and its possible relation to dark matter.
arxiv-2411-15307.creator: Frode K. Hansen, Diego Garcia Lambas, Heliana E. Luparello, Facundo Toscano, Luis A. Pereyra
arxiv-2411-15307.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frode K. Hansen, Diego Garcia Lambas, Heliana E. Luparello, Facundo Toscano, Luis A. Pereyra. We confirm at the 5.7 ​ σ 5.7\sigma level previous studies reporting Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) temperatures being significantly lower around nearby spiral galaxies than expected in the Λ \Lambda CDM model.

arxiv-2503-09795.title: Bounds on Independent Isolation in Graphs
arxiv-2503-09795.description: Abstract An isolating set of a graph is a set of vertices S S such that, if S S and its neighborhood is removed, only isolated vertices remain; and the isolation number is the minimum size of such a set.

arxiv-2505-16568.title: Arf rings, simple singularities and reflexive modules
arxiv-2505-16568.creator: Özgür Esentepe
arxiv-2505-16568.description: Abstract . In a pandemic era preprint, Dao showed showed two remarkable properties of Arf rings: under some mild conditions, they admit finitely many indecomposable reflexive modules up to isomorphism and every reflexive module is actually isomorphic to its own dual. In fact, the latter property characterises Arf rings.

arxiv-2505-20002.title: Efficient Gaussian Mixture Filters based on Transition Density Approximation The work was partially supported by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic under project ROBOPROX - Robotics and Advanced Industrial Production CZ.02.01.01/00/22_008/0004590.
arxiv-2505-20002.creator: Ondřej Straka, Uwe D. Hanebeck, Intelligent Sensor-Actuator-Systems Laboratory (ISAS) Karlsruhe Institute of Technology Karlsruhe, Germany E-mail: uwe.hanebeck@kit.edu
arxiv-2505-20002.description: Abstract Gaussian mixture filters for nonlinear systems usually rely on severe approximations when calculating mixtures in the prediction and filtering step. Thus, offline approximations of noise densities by Gaussian mixture densities to reduce the approximation error have been proposed. This results in exponential growth in the number of components, requiring ongoing component reduction, which is computationally complex.

arxiv-2506-07882.title: Evaluating Explainable AI for Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection System Alert Classification
arxiv-2506-07882.creator: Rajesh Kalakoti, Risto Vaarandi, Hayretdin Bahşi, Sven Nõmm
arxiv-2506-07882.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rajesh Kalakoti, Risto Vaarandi, Hayretdin Bahşi, Sven Nõmm. A Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) monitors networks for cyber attacks and other unwanted activities. However, NIDS solutions often generate an overwhelming number of alerts daily, making it challenging for analysts to prioritize high-priority threats. While deep learning models promise to automate the prioritization of NIDS alerts, the lack of transparency in these models can undermine trust in their decision-making.

arxiv-2507-07007.title: Robust signal decompositions on the circle
arxiv-2507-07007.creator: Aral Köse, Daniel Liberzon
arxiv-2507-07007.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aral Köse, Daniel Liberzon. We consider the problem of decomposing a piecewise constant function on the circle into a sum of indicator functions of closed circular disks in the plane, whose number and location are not a priori known.

arxiv-2512-17181.title: On-Demand Millisecond Storage of Spectro-Temporal Multimode Telecom Photons
arxiv-2512-17181.creator: Anuj Sethia, Nasser Gohari Kamel, Daniel Oblak
arxiv-2512-17181.description: Abstract The realization of scalable quantum networks for distribution of entanglement over long distances hinges on quantum repeaters. To outperform the exponential transmission loss in optical fibers, quantum repeaters must employ multiplexing schemes in the temporal, spectral, or spatial domain.

arxiv-2602-16924.title: Overdamped limits for Langevin dynamics with position-dependent coefficients via L 2 L^{2} -hypocoercivity
arxiv-2602-16924.creator: Noé Blassel
arxiv-2602-16924.description: Abstract This note provides a simple derivation of the overdamped approximation for kinetic (or underdamped) equilibrium Langevin dynamics, in cases where certain coefficients depend on the position variable. The equivalent small-mass limit of these dynamics, known as the Kramers–Smoluchowski approximation, in the case of a state-dependent friction coefficient, has been previously studied by a variety of approaches.

plos-pone-0009573.creator: Simon J. Greenhill, Alexei J. Drummond, Russell D. Gray
plos-pone-0009573.description: PLOS ONE research article. We recently used computational phylogenetic methods on lexical data to test between two scenarios for the peopling of the Pacific. pmc-10496407.title: PhaseDancer: a novel targeted assembler of segmental duplications unravels the complexity of the human chromosome 2 fusion going from 48 to 46 chromosomes in hominin evolution
pmc-10496407.creator: Barbara Poszewiecka, Krzysztof Gogolewski, Justyna A Karolak, Paweł Stankiewicz, Anna Gambin
pmc-10496407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Resolving complex genomic regions rich in segmental duplications (SDs) is challenging due to the high error rate of long-read sequencing. Here, we describe a targeted approach with a novel genome assembler PhaseDancer that extends SD-rich regions of interest iteratively. We validate its robustness and efficiency using a golden-standard set of human BAC clones and in silico-generated SDs with predefined evolutionary scenarios.

pmc-10615462.title: A primary pediatric acute myelomonocytic leukemia with t(3;21)(q26;q22): A case report
pmc-10615462.creator: Jia-xin Duan, Fang Liu, Li Chang, Guang-lu Che, Qiu-xia Yang, Jie Teng, Hui Jian, Xiao-juan Liu, Shu-yu Lai
pmc-10615462.description: Rationale:The rare t(3;21)(q26;q22) translocation results in gene fusion and generates multiple fusion transcripts, which are typically associated with therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, and chronic myelogenous leukemia. Here, we report a rare case of de novo acute myelomonocytic leukemia in a young child with t(3;21)(q26;q22).

Vaccines offer a promising alternative for controlling bacterial infections in pigs, but their widespread use is often hindered by biological, economic, and practical challenges. This study surveyed U.S.

pmc-12721402.title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding tuberculosis in a low-incidence area in the USA
pmc-12721402.creator: Jenna Randall, Nicole Kelp
pmc-12721402.description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a large global health threat, including increasing cases in generally low-incidence areas of the USA. However, the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) regarding TB in these low-incidence areas are underexplored, precluding planning for effective health communication in these areas regarding travel to high-incidence areas or potential future outbreaks in currently low-incidence areas.

pmc-12879055.title: Genome-wide identification and analysis of expression of pathogenesis-related protein 1 (PR-1) gene family in brown algae
pmc-12879055.creator: Linhong Teng, Shuxia Liang, Jiayi Chen, Bostjan Kobe, Naihao Ye, Hui Wang, Jian Song
pmc-12879055.description: The pathogen-related protein 1 (PR-1) family plays an important role in plant response to biotic and abiotic stresses. PR-1 proteins have been studied in many plant species; however, they were not systematically studied in brown algae, which are important components of coastal ecosystems and have great economic value in the aquaculture industry.

pmc-13052541.title: Adherence to ART medication refill pick-up in the regional hospital HIV clinics at the Sekhukhune district in Limpopo province, South Africa: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13052541.creator: Mulisa Nepfumbada, Anam Nyembezi
pmc-13052541.description: IntroductionSouth Africa has been reported to have a high burden of HIV and is currently running the largest anti-retroviral treatment (ART) programme globally which incorporates the test and treat policy. However, adherence to ART is particularly crucial for the optimal health outcomes of HIV patients. Evidence revealed that there are barriers to medication adherence in many parts of the country.

It remains unclear whether these compounds exert immunomodulatory effects that contribute to their behavioural and clinical efficacy while maintaining a favourable safety profile.
